q1.explanationZh: 女孩本来申请了给动物喂食，后来想到问能不能当导游带游客参观，园方同意了（they agreed）。B 喂食是她起初的想法，后来改了；A 看爸爸给猴子喂药是以前的事，而且她当时什么都不能做。

q2.explanationZh: 犯罪小说和科幻小说都太贵，男孩买了一本讲几个人去不同的山上探险的小说（travel to different mountains looking for adventures）。C 犯罪小说他打算以后攒钱再买；A 科幻小说更贵，没买。

q3.explanationZh: Anna 的妈妈会开车送她回家（her mum’s offered to give me a lift back），她说这比坐火车方便多了。B 她没坐火车；A 她不想天黑骑车，把自行车留在学校，明天再骑回去。

q4.explanationZh: 男孩没时间吃鸡蛋和吐司，想拿香蕉和苹果，但已经没有了；妈妈说有麦片，他说只要有牛奶就吃麦片，妈妈说牛奶很多（there’s plenty）。B 他没时间吃；C 水果已经吃完了。

q5.explanationZh: 男孩说刚上完美术课，女孩说课间休息后她要上的就是这门课（That’s what I’ve got after this break）。B 地理是她刚上完的课；A 数学要到午饭后才上。

q6.explanationZh: 爸爸给了她 30 英镑，她找回 12.50 英镑，所以墨镜只花了 17.50 英镑（you only paid seventeen pounds fifty）。A 12.50 是找回的零钱；C 29.50 是打折前的原价。

q7.explanationZh: 男孩的公交车停在购物中心旁，他提议在那里见面，女孩最后说就在他建议的地方见（let’s meet where you suggested），即购物中心旁的车站。B 咖啡馆是女孩和妈妈吃午饭的地方；C 游泳池是妈妈带弟弟去的地方。

q8.explanationZh: 女孩说车上人多，非常热，哥哥说热得想脱夹克却没地方脱，两人都抱怨车里太热。A 只有哥哥抱怨一路站着，妹妹说她不介意；B 他们没有抱怨别的乘客，反而担心自己的音乐吵到了别人。

q9.explanationZh: 男孩说历史片太长、没什么动作场面，爱情喜剧总是老一套，他担心这些电影会无聊。A 他觉得科幻片听起来很刺激，并不犹豫；C 有三种电影可选，他没有对选择感到失望。

q10.explanationZh: 女孩说不敢相信咖啡馆的果汁和柠檬水这么贵，比别的地方都贵（More than other places）。A 她想放学后去游泳，但那时泳池总是关闭，时间并不方便；B 她只说吹风机不错，没说更衣室很现代。

q11.explanationZh: 男孩对女孩说“你会喜欢的（You’d love it）”，并建议她考虑加入，即认为她会喜欢参加这个俱乐部。B 难的实验是以后才做，目前还没做什么；C 他提到了新老师，但没说老师好。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩说本来希望营地离海更近一些，而且海滩附近没有停车场，只能走过去，所以对营地的位置感到失望。B 每晚有表演，他和别的孩子玩得很开心；C 他说可以打迷你高尔夫、攀岩，营地在这方面更好。

q13.explanationZh: 妈妈因为他疼给了他几片药，吃完以后就好了（It was fine after that）。C 他受不了任何东西碰到胳膊，所以没包绷带；A 他说服妈妈不用去看医生。

q14.explanationZh: Victor 说他们选的船叫 Silver Star（The one we chose was called Silver Star）；Golden Sun 是另一艘更大的船，他想下次再坐。

q15.explanationZh: Victor 说三个半小时对他们来说正好（Three and a half hours was enough for us）；10 小时和 1.5 小时是别的船的航程。

q16.explanationZh: 他们去的时候不是看鲸鱼的季节，但有一群可爱的海豚游到了船边（a lovely group of dolphins came very close to us），所以填 dolphins，不填 whales。

q17.explanationZh: 岛上的悬崖很壮观，但更棒的是山洞（even better were the caves），他们还走进了几个山洞；空格要填他特别喜欢的地方，所以不是 cliffs。

q18.explanationZh: 船长说一月份不要去，因为天气很差，船员都在休假（avoid going in January）；九月是最佳时间，二月船员就回来了。

q19.explanationZh: 网址是 www.robshaw.islandboattrips.com，Victor 逐个字母拼出了 R-O-B-S-H-A-W。

q20.explanationZh: Amy 说 11 岁时因为重感冒没去上学（off school with a bad cold），在网上看到博主们谈做视频博客，于是有了这个想法。A 她是在网上看到博主，不是见面；B 当时她没在学校。

q21.explanationZh: Amy 说刚上传的最新一期讲的是一种据说对身体很好的酸奶（a kind of yoghurt），即一种健康食品。A、C 边听音乐锻炼边试穿运动鞋是下一期的内容。

q22.explanationZh: Amy 说保持平静最重要，所以录制前会安静地坐一会儿（sit quietly for a bit），即花时间放松。A 她不太在意穿什么；C 她会看笔记，但不会照着念，也尽量不去担心要说什么。

q23.explanationZh: Amy 说即使不发博客的日子，她也会和在视频评论区留言的人交流，这是每天都做的事（That’s a daily event），即回复粉丝的留言。B 她只是在社交媒体上放链接；C 她说博客不像私人日记。

q24.explanationZh: Amy 说最喜欢和那些想让地球变得更好的人交谈（people that want to make the planet a better place），即想改变世界的人。B 体育冠军很好聊，但不是她的最爱；C 她提到青少年，是说喜欢重视青少年意见的人。

q25.explanationZh: Amy 说想让粉丝看到她真实的性格，不要以为她很完美（so they don’t think I’m perfect），即表明自己是个普通人。C 她喜欢自嘲，但没说是为了逗粉丝笑；A 她说做视频博客不只是为了受欢迎，没提吸引新观众。

content.v: Test Three. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now look at the instructions for Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. What is the girl going to do this summer?
I’m going to be a volunteer in our school holidays!
Cool! I heard the wildlife park’s looking for people to feed the animals.

Yeah! I thought about that and I applied for it. Then I thought, ‘Why don’t I ask if I can be a guide showing visitors round?’ and they agreed. I know loads about the animals cos my dad’s a vet there. I went to the park once to watch him giving medicine to some monkeys – I wasn’t allowed to do anything, but I’d love to be a vet, too, one day.
Two. Which book did the boy buy?
Did you get a new book when you went to the bookstore today?
Yeah, I did, Mum. I saw a really interesting crime novel. And there was a brilliant science-fiction one, too. I really wanted to get both of them!
Oh? So what did you buy in the end?

Well, they were both fairly expensive, especially the science-fiction one. Instead, I found a novel based on a true story about some guys who travel to different mountains looking for adventures. I’m going to save up for the crime novel.
Great!
Three. How will the girl get home from school today?

Mum, I’m phoning to say I’m staying after school today to help get the stage ready for tomorrow’s concert. A few of us are. Anna’s staying too, and her mum’s offered to give me a lift back as I know you’ll be busy later, and it’d be a lot easier than catching the train. You know how I feel about cycling in the dark. I’ll leave my bike here. I think it’ll be quite late when we finish … so I’ll ride it back tomorrow afternoon. Anyway, see you later. Bye!
Four. What will the boy eat for breakfast?
Do you fancy egg and toast this morning, Ben? You should have a good breakfast before football practice.
I’d love that, Mum. I don’t think I’ll have time, though. I’ll just grab a banana and an apple.
Well, you won’t be able to, as there are none left! There’s some cereal, though.
Looks like I’ll have to have that then … if we’ve got any milk?
Oh, yes, there’s plenty. Don’t worry.
Will you get some more fruit when you go out?
Sure. I know you love it!
Five. Which lesson has the girl got next?
How was your last lesson?
Oh, OK. We were studying all about mountains and rivers in geography. It was quite interesting.
Oh, all about water then? I’ve just had art, not my favourite, as you know. We had to draw a man’s face. I’m not very good at art.
That’s what I’ve got after this break. It’s one of my favourite subjects. I find it much more enjoyable than maths. I’ve got that straight after lunch.
Oh, well, nearly time to go …
Six. How much were the girl’s new sunglasses?
I got my new sunglasses, Dad!
So I see – they look really nice! Is there any change from the money I gave you?
Yes, here you are – twelve pounds fifty.
Thanks … Oh, I wasn’t expecting to get quite so much back. I gave you thirty pounds, so that means you only paid seventeen pounds fifty for them.
Yes, they normally cost twenty-nine pounds fifty, but they were reduced in the sale.
That’s great. They look really good on you.
Seven. Where are the friends going to meet?
Is your mum bringing you into town when we meet tomorrow?
Yes, she’s going to drive me there in the car on her way to the swimming pool – she’s taking my brother for his lesson.
Great. My bus stops by the shopping centre. How about we meet there? We could spend the whole morning there, and maybe get something to eat?
Well, I’m meeting my mum for lunch in a café actually. You could join us, but, anyway, let’s meet where you suggested.
OK. That all sounds great.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear a brother and sister talking about a train journey.
Phew! I’m glad we’re off that train now!
Me too! What a nightmare having to stand all the way.
I didn’t mind that – but it was really hot with all those people on board, wasn’t it?
It made me want to take my jacket off, but there was no room. At least, we had something to listen to, to pass the time. I’m glad we’d downloaded that new music before we left home.
… yeah, but the people standing next to us didn’t seem too happy. I think they could hear it. I felt a bit guilty about that.
Yeah, me too.
Nine. You will hear two friends talking about going to the cinema.
What’s on at the cinema at the moment?
Let’s see … That historical film you were talking about, a romantic comedy and a science-fiction film.

Well, we should choose the historical film because it’s about what we’re studying at school. It’s really long though, and it doesn’t have much action. And romantic comedies are always the same kind of stories! What’s the science-fiction film about?
A journey through space. Sounds like it might be good?
Well, it sounds quite exciting. Shall we see that?
Yeah, OK. I agree.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about a new swimming pool.
Have you been to the new swimming pool?
Yes, last Sunday.
I went on Saturday. I’d really like to go for a swim after school, but it always seems to be closed for private swimming lessons then.
I think it opens again later on weekdays for people who go after work. I was impressed by the changing rooms – the showers are great.

They’ve got good hairdryers, too. I also went to the café there. I couldn’t believe the price of juice and lemonade. More than other places. The food looked delicious, though, and it’s open every day.
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about an after-school science club.
We had our first after-school science club today. That new teacher’s in charge of it.
Oh, right. What kinds of things did you do?

Well, not much yet, but the teacher was telling us about all the experiments we’ll do, and they sound quite difficult, but you’re really into science. You’d love it. If you haven’t decided which club to go to yet, you should think about joining.
I’ll make up my mind soon. Anyway, you’ve made me think about it seriously, but I want to ask my brother which one he’s going to join.
OK.
Twelve. You will hear a boy telling a friend about a family camping holiday he went on.
How was your holiday?

We went to a different campsite this year – we’d all got a bit bored with the usual place. This new one looked much better on the website, and it was in some ways, like you could do mini-golf and climbing. I was hoping it’d be nearer the sea than it was, though. There was no car park near the beach, so we had to walk.
What did you do in the evening?
There was a show each night, but I mostly played things like table tennis with other kids I’d met there, which was fun.
Thirteen. You will hear two friends talking about an accident the boy had.
How did you hurt your arm?
I slipped down the stairs at home and hit it as I fell.
Oh, dear.

Yeah, I was lucky not to break it. My mum tried to wrap it in a bandage, but I couldn’t stand anything touching it. It was almost time for bed, so Mum gave me a few pills because of the pain. It was fine after that. She still wanted to take me to the doctor in the morning, but I persuaded her that there was no need, even if I did have to use my other arm more that day.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a boy called Victor giving a class presentation about a boat trip he went on.

Hi, everyone. I want to tell you about a boat trip I went on recently. My mum drove us to a little port called Seaville. There were loads of boats there taking people on trips. Their names all had connections with things in the sky. The one we chose was called Silver Star. There was a much bigger one called Golden Sun that I’d like to go on another time.
You can choose how long you want to go on a boat trip for. Three and a half hours was enough for us, but some boats go out for as much as ten hours, and others as little as an hour and a half.

You can see all sorts of things from the boat. At certain times of year, you might be lucky enough to see whales as they swim up the coast. We went at the wrong time for that, but a lovely group of dolphins came very close to us.

We visited an island as part of the trip. There were some amazing cliffs, which looked very high, but even better were the caves there. They had lights in and we walked into several of them for a few hundred metres.

If you’d like to go on a boat trip there, the captain of our boat said the best time to visit is in September. There’s lots of wildlife around then, but avoid going in January as that’s when the weather’s really bad, and the crews all take their holidays. They’re usually back by February.

You can find out more by going to the website that has all the information on boat trips. The address is www dot robshaw dot islandboattrips dot com. I’ll spell that for you … it’s R-O-B-S-H-A-W dot islandboattrips dot com.
Thanks for listening!
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a young woman called Amy Wu, who makes video blogs and uploads them to the internet.
We have a video blogger on the show today – someone who records and appears in their own videos on the internet. Amy Wu, who’s only 19, has a popular video blog. Welcome, Amy.
Hi.
So how did you get the idea of becoming a video blogger?

I was 11, and I was off school with a bad cold. Because I was bored, I went online to find something for one of the lessons I was missing. On one website, some video bloggers were talking about making their blogs. I thought … I’m sure I could produce one people my age’d like to watch, so I did. I didn’t know then it’d be such a success.
What sort of thing’s your blog about?

Well, I do lots of stuff about health and fitness, so I’m often asked by companies to review their products. In my next one, for example, I’m trying out a pair of trainers while exercising to music. That’ll be more fun than the latest one I’ve just uploaded to the internet. It was about a kind of yoghurt which is supposed to be really good for you.
So what do you do before you record your video blog?

I don’t think too much about what I wear, and I try not to worry about what I’ll say. I check my notes, but I avoid reading them aloud as I want to sound totally natural. Feeling calm’s essential, so I sit quietly for a bit. Then I feel ready to record.
Are there some things you have to do every day?

Well, the blog isn’t like a personal diary – I don’t blog every day. But when I do, I put links on my social media pages. Even on days when I don’t post a blog, I communicate with anyone who’s said something in the comments section of my videos. That’s a daily event.
You also interview people on your blog …

Yes, I’ve interviewed some famous sports champions. I find them really easy to talk to. But they’re not my favourite. I really like talking to people that want to make the planet a better place, especially if they’re interested in the opinions of teenagers like me, because we’re the future.
You made one blog called ‘My Mistakes’ …

Oh, that … Video blogging isn’t just about being popular. I like my fans to see my true character so they don’t think I’m perfect. I enjoy the silly moments, like when I pronounce something incorrectly. And I also like laughing at myself. It helps me not take everything too seriously.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
